prompt: Create one continuous 10-second photoreal novel-view shot of the SAME STATIC physical scene. @Image1 is a real photograph, uniformly scaled and cropped, of the STARTING camera view. It is the authority for object identity, observed construction, materials, colors, lighting, and scene details. It is NOT a character sheet, flat backdrop, or frame to repeat. @Video1 is a procedural geometric reconstruction of that SAME scene. Follow its camera translation, local arc, framing progression, relative depth and changing occlusion. Replace its simplified CG surfaces with the real photographed appearance from @Image1; do not copy low-poly shading or transform the scene into a cartoon. Scene identity: A stationary round wooden outdoor table with radial tabletop boards, upright legs and diagonal/cross bracing on paved ground. A weathered brown vase holds a dry fan-shaped leaf at its center. A green-and-black ball rests beneath it. Grass, layered plants, brick walls, a dark door, and distant roof shapes surround the scene. Camera route: One uninterrupted 360-degree counterclockwise world-space orbit over exactly ten seconds. Analytic bearing velocity varies smoothly from 32.23 to 39.77 degrees per second. Radius grows from 4.50 to 5.20 units and the camera cranes 0.84 units up for the rear reveal, then flows down and inward into a still-moving source-side bearing. Fixed 37.2-degree FOV; no digital zoom, destination or hold. The last encoded frame at 9.9667s reaches 358.674 degrees; the continuous path completes 360 only at the ten-second boundary.  KINETIC CAMERA CONTRACT: @Video1 has highest authority for continuous camera motion. @Image1 controls appearance only and must not anchor, slow, recenter or stop the camera. Camera intent: Maintain the entire stationary table/vase/fan assembly as an anchor while translating through strong foreground-foot, ball, tabletop, planting and wall parallax. Use a rising outward arc to expose the radial boards and support topology, then a continuous descending return that never stops. SINGLE-BALL IDENTITY AND RIGIDITY: exactly one small green-and-black ball exists, present from the opening frame at its fixed authored location on the paving beneath the table, adjacent to the crossed ground rails; its world center is (0.095, 0.126, -0.240) with radius 0.120 scene units. This is the same existing photographed ball throughout the entire orbit, never a new object revealed by transformation. Preserve its spherical volume, size, fixed world orientation, green rubber and attached black pentagonal panels. The ball stays rigid and stationary: it never rolls, spins, rotates, translates, inflates, grows, shrinks, deforms or morphs. Its screen position, apparent size and visible panel faces may change only through the authored moving-camera perspective and occlusion by the stationary table supports. Occlusion never deletes the ball; maintain its identity and location behind each support and reveal that same ball again. No object may appear, grow, morph or rotate into an additional ball. Do not invent, duplicate or split balls, and do not convert stones, tiny flower parts, the vase's dark scar, metal bolts, paving marks, shadows, supports or background planters into balls. Preserve the complete static surrounding garden, ground, walls, foliage and furniture; only the camera moves. Travel continuously through one 360-degree counterclockwise path over all ten seconds. Screen-space travel: The camera initially trucks toward the garden right around the table while looking back toward its center. The original left door and rear ivy sweep rightward behind the anchored vase, the near table legs exchange overlaps with the ball, and the far garden rotates into view before the original wall returns through the opposite side. There is no destination framing and no final hold: every second must contain strong world-space camera displacement, parallax and changing occlusion. Required camera beats: (1) 0-2.5s — leave the source view immediately, sliding right with gentle lift; the nearest leg traverses the green ball and the left-hand door sweeps right behind the tabletop and vase before leaving the view. (2) 2.5-5s — continue through the side into a wider, higher rear reveal; the fan becomes edge-on and reverses its folds while the crossed basal rails untangle against lawn. (3) 5-7.5s — keep sweeping around the inferred far garden; the rear of the vase and complete tabletop circumference remain anchored while planting and wall reverse their overlaps. (4) 7.5-10s — descend and dolly inward through the opposite side; the original door/roof return behind the fan and front braces sweep across the ball, still moving at the final sample. Required changing-occlusion evidence: (1) The green-and-black ball begins behind the front cross-rail, passes behind a square leg near the first quarter orbit, and is exposed from the rear as the near/far rails exchange order. (2) The vase overlaps a dark ivy gap in the source, separates from the original rear wall at the side, and silhouettes against inferred near-garden planting halfway around. (3) The radial tabletop begins as a shallow ellipse; the crane makes its center disc and wedge seams more visible during the far-side arc before the descending return restores the shallow view. (4) The black door begins at the far-left crop edge, crosses rightward behind the table during the first quadrant and returns through the opposite side in the final moving quadrant. The right planter separates from the dry fan with deeper layered parallax. Never settle into a hero frame, pause for the action, reverse direction, rotate the subject as a turntable, or replace physical camera travel with digital zoom/pan.  GRAY MODEL VIDEO ENCODING: @Video1 is a neutral gray shaded model with no valid color, texture or material identity. Use its continuous surface volume, normals, silhouette, camera, perspective, support and occlusion as strict geometry guidance. @Image1 is the appearance authority. Replace all gray surfaces with authentic photographic materials and lighting; never output gray clay, CGI, miniature or viewport-render appearance. Begin at the photographed source composition, then reveal a coherent local novel view with clear foreground/background parallax. Only the camera moves; keep all physical objects and materials fixed. The table, vase, dry fan leaf and green ball remain rigidly stationary. Preserve the round tabletop, radial wood divisions, supports and ball position. Do not replace the dry fan leaf with a living plant or add people. The real photograph and proxy share the same centered 4:3 aspect-ratio crop. Preserve that crop without stretching, zooming past it, or inventing scene content outside the photographed crop. Complete newly revealed surfaces conservatively from the observed scene; Do not add, remove, morph, duplicate, rotate or animate objects.
